raw_symptom_text: A leaf spot symptom initially appeared as grey-green and/or water soaked with a darker green border and then expanded rapidly to several centimeters in length and became light tan in color with a distinct necrotic border.
location: Ord River Irrigation Area in northern Western Australia
citation: You et al. (2012). First Report of Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) on Rice (Oryza sativa) in Western Australia. Plant Disease, 96(8): 1228-1228.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms observed in commercial fields during September and October consisted mainly of darkened lesions at the panicle neck node and flag leaf collar. Many of the panicles with neck rot were partially filled or blank.
location: Sacramento Valley of California
citation: Greer et al. (1997). First Report of Rice Blast Caused by Pyricularia grisea in California. Plant Disease, 81(9): 1094-1094.

raw_symptom_text: Typical symptoms were characterized by yellow to grayish, water-soaked lesions that start from the leaf tip and progress along the central vein or leaf margin. At an advanced stage of the disease, the leaves were completely desiccated sometimes with droplets of yellow exudate at the leaf margin.
location: Vakinankaratra, the Central Highlands of Madagascar
citation: Raveloson et al. (2023). First Report of Bacterial Leaf Blight Disease of Rice Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae in Madagascar. Plant Disease, 107(8): 2510.

raw_symptom_text: Galls and hooked tips were found in the roots of rice seedlings and plants.
location: Guanghan City, Sichuan Province, Southwest China
citation: Xie et al. (2019). First Report of Root-Knot Nematode, Meloidogyne graminicola, on Rice in Sichuan Province, Southwest China. Plant Disease, 103(8): 2142-2142.

raw_symptom_text: A few spikelets in a panicle transform into globose, yellowish green, velvety spore balls that are 2 to 5 cm in diameter and covered by a thin orange membrane. The membrane bursts open and releases powdery dark green spores.
location: Rice Research Station at Crowley, LA
citation: Rush et al. (2000). Outbreak of False Smut of Rice in Louisiana. Plant Disease, 84(1): 100-100.

raw_symptom_text: Besides blight symptoms and water-soaked lesions in the leaves, the most noticeable symptom observed was the blackening or darkening of the leaf tips, which appeared as dark spots or streaks. In panicles, panicle blight-like symptoms, such as grain discoloration and darkening of rice hulls, were observed.
location: Louisiana
citation: Bruno et al. (2025). First Report of Xanthomonas sacchari Causing Bacterial Panicle Blight of Rice in the United States. Plant Disease, 109(11): 2426.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms were variable, appearing as either (i) oblong pale to dark brown lesions up to 3 cm length, (ii) lesions with pale grey/brown centers and with dark brown margins, or (iii) diffuse dark or reddish brown streaks along the sheath. Lesions enlarged and coalesced, often covering the majority of the leaf sheath, disrupting panicle emergence.
location: Ord River Irrigation Area (ORIA) in northern Western Australia
citation: Lanoiselet et al. (2012). First Report of Sarocladium oryzae Causing Sheath Rot on Rice (Oryza sativa) in Western Australia. Plant Disease, 96(9): 1382-1382.

raw_symptom_text: During a survey carried out in April of 2013, severe symptoms characterized by seedling death, severe plant malformation, and foliar striping were observed on rice plants in an experimental field of INERA at Banfora located in western Burkina Faso.
location: Banfora located in western Burkina Faso
citation: Sereme et al. (2014). First Report of Rice stripe necrosis virus Infecting Rice in Burkina Faso. Plant Disease, 98(10): 1451-1451.

raw_symptom_text: In September 2012, plants with leaf yellowing and mottling symptoms were observed near Bahir Dar and in the Fogera district in the northwestern part of the country during a joint survey of scientists from Madagascar (FOFIFA), Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR), and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).
location: near Bahir Dar and in the Fogera district
citation: Rakotomalala et al. (2014). First Report of Rice yellow mottle virus in Rice in Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. Plant Disease, 98(10): 1449-1449.

raw_symptom_text: In October 2011, plants with leaf yellowing and mottling symptoms were observed in large irrigated rice production schemes about 30 km west of Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, and in lowland subsistence fields in Bangui outskirts.
location: Bangui, Central African Republic
citation: Longué et al. (2014). First Report of Rice yellow mottle virus in Rice in the Central African Republic. Plant Disease, 98(1): 162-162.

raw_symptom_text: Infected plants showed yellowing stripe symptoms on leaves.
location: Vietnam
citation: Ren et al. (2013). First Report of Rice stripe virus in Vietnam. Plant Disease, 97(8): 1123-1123.

raw_symptom_text: In July 2012, plants with leaf yellowing and mottling symptoms were observed in large irrigated rice production schemes 30 km south of Bukavu, in eastern DRC, and in lowland subsistence fields in the surroundings of Bukavu.
location: Bukavu, in eastern DRC
citation: Hubert et al. (2013). First Report of Rice yellow mottle virus on Rice in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Plant Disease, 97(12): 1664-1664.

raw_symptom_text: Plants with symptoms of black, circular, necrotic spots 3 to 4 mm in diameter and an average of 8 to 10 spots per leaf were observed.
location: Pakistan
citation: Akhtar et al. (2014). First Report of Rice Leaf Spot by Alternaria gaisen from Pakistan. Plant Disease, 98(10): 1440-1440.

raw_symptom_text: In July 2012, symptoms consisting of circular, black, necrotic spots, 2 to 4 mm in diameter, were observed on leaves of a commonly grown rice cultivar, Basmati-198, in private rice fields at Lahore (Punjab).
location: Lahore (Punjab)
citation: Akhtar et al. (2014). First Report of Leaf Spot of Rice Caused by Alternaria arborescens in Pakistan. Plant Disease, 98(6): 846-846.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms in rice plantations of Palestina city, like upright panicles with grayish-straw color, grain rot, and vain grains were observed in July 2013, although similar symptoms were first noticed as early as 2012 in other regions of Ecuador.
location: Palestina city, Ecuador
citation: Riera-Ruiz et al. (2014). First Report of Bacterial Panicle Blight of Rice Caused by Burkholderia gladioli in Ecuador. Plant Disease, 98(11): 1577-1577.

raw_symptom_text: Typical symptoms started as green water-soaked streaks from the tip or edge of leaf blades, similar to bacterial leaf blight caused by Xanthomonas oryzae. Infected leaves turned yellow, then eventually became wilted and dry.
location: Zhejiang Province, China
citation: Liu et al. (2014). First Report of Leaf Blight of Rice Caused by Cochliobolus lunatus in China. Plant Disease, 98(5): 686-686.

raw_symptom_text: In 2007, leaf mottling, reduced tillering, and stunting symptoms were observed on rice at Gatumba near Bujumbura, causing small patches in less than 10% of the fields.
location: Gatumba near Bujumbura, Burundi
citation: Ndikumana et al. (2012). First Report of Rice yellow mottle virus on Rice in Burundi. Plant Disease, 96(8): 1230-1230.

raw_symptom_text: Rice plantations showing BPB-like symptoms including upright panicles with stained and vain grains were spotted in Palestina city, one of Ecuador's most extensive rice areas, in July 2013, but similar symptoms have been observed in the region since early 2012.
location: Palestina city, Ecuador
citation: Riera-Ruiz et al. (2014). First Report of Burkholderia glumae Causing Bacterial Panicle Blight on Rice in Ecuador. Plant Disease, 98(7): 988-988.

raw_symptom_text: Leaf tips of susceptible rice varieties were white or yellow, becoming brown or black as necrosis set in. Tips of developing leaves were twisted and wrinkled. The flag leaf became twisted above the panicle until development was inhibited. General stunting of the plant accompanied leaf injury.
location: cities of Changchun and Gongzhuling, Jinlin Province, China
citation: Ou et al. (2014). First Report of Aphelenchoides besseyi Causing White Tip Disease of Rice in Jilin Province, China. Plant Disease, 98(8): 1165-1165.

raw_symptom_text: Affected leaves showed typical BLS symptoms, such as water-soaked lesions, translucent stripes, and yellow-brown to black streaks, sometimes with visible exudates at the leaf surfaces.
location: Doho, Nambale, and Magada, Uganda
citation: Afolabi et al. (2014). First Report of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola Causing Bacterial Leaf Streak of Rice in Uganda. Plant Disease, 98(11): 1579-1579.

raw_symptom_text: Affected leaves showed water-soaked translucent lesions and yellow-brown to black streaks, sometimes with visible exudates on leaf surfaces.
location: Musenyi, Gihanga, and Rugombo fields in Burundi
citation: Afolabi et al. (2014). First Report of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola Causing Bacterial Leaf Streak of Rice in Burundi. Plant Disease, 98(10): 1426-1426.

raw_symptom_text: Affected panicles contained florets that initially exhibited discoloration ranging from light green to light brown on the basal portion of the glumes and later developed a reddish-brown margin separating this area from the rest of the glume that became straw-colored.
location: Ukulima farm in Limpopo Province, South Africa
citation: Zhou et al. (2014). First Report of Bacterial Panicle Blight of Rice Caused by Burkholderia glumae in South Africa. Plant Disease, 98(4): 566-566.

raw_symptom_text: The typical symptom was a dark brown decay of the tillers. In the early stages of the disease, a brown sheath rot seemed to spread from the ligulae regions.
location: Guangdong Province, China
citation: Pu et al. (2012). First Report of Bacterial Foot Rot of Rice Caused by a Dickeya zeae in China. Plant Disease, 96(12): 1818-1818.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms consisted of a generic seedling wilt, a root length reduction ranging from 21 to 48%, and the presence of root discoloration.
location: Modena, northern Italy
citation: Prà et al. (2010). First Report of Fusarium andiyazi Associated with Rice Bakanae in Italy. Plant Disease, 94(8): 1070-1070.

raw_symptom_text: Lesions appeared first as water-soaked stripes or light brown-to-slightly reddish spots on the upper blades of the leaves, ultimately causing leaf blight and stalk rot.
location: Gwangyang and Naju, Jeonnam Province, Korea
citation: Lee et al. (2010). First Report of Leaf Blight Caused by Pantoea agglomerans on Rice in Korea. Plant Disease, 94(11): 1372-1372.

raw_symptom_text: In countries in westernmost Africa (The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Mauritania, and Senegal), plants with leaf yellowing and mottling symptoms were observed, but RYMV was never isolated.
location: Kuntaur Region in the center of The Gambia
citation: Sere et al. (2008). First Report of Rice yellow mottle virus in Rice in The Gambia. Plant Disease, 92(2): 316-316.

raw_symptom_text: Lesions usually appeared on lower leaves and were approximately 2 to 7 mm long and linear with whitish or grayish centers surrounded by a narrow brown-or-dark brown margin.
location: Beaumont, TX
citation: Zhou et al. (2010). First Report of White Leaf Streak of Rice Caused by Mycovellosiella oryzae in Texas. Plant Disease, 94(5): 639-639.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms consisted of water-soaked lesions that developed into translucent, yellow streaks with visible exudates at the leaf surface.
location: Haut-Bassin, Cascades, and East Center, Burkina Faso
citation: Wonni et al. (2011). First Report of Bacterial Leaf Streak Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola on Rice in Burkina Faso. Plant Disease, 95(1): 72-72.

raw_symptom_text: During July 2000, plants with leaf yellowing and mottling symptoms were observed in Uganda in a subsistence rice field northeast of Lake Victoria, close to the Nile River.
location: northeast of Lake Victoria, close to the Nile River, Uganda
citation: Pinel-Galzi et al. (2006). First Report of Rice yellow mottle virus in Rice in Uganda. Plant Disease, 90(5): 683-683.

raw_symptom_text: Diseased seedlings showed water-soaked areas on coleoptiles and brown stripes on leaf sheaths and mid-ribs.
location: Burkina Faso
citation: Somda et al. (2001). First Report on the Occurrence of Bacterial Stripe Organism Acidovorax avenae subsp. avenae in Rice Seeds from Burkina Faso. Plant Disease, 85(7): 804-804.

raw_symptom_text: About 5% of plants exhibited symptoms, characterized by chlorosis starting from the tips of the leaves and spreading towards the base, turning into bleached, necrotic lesions with wavy margins. As the disease advanced, the lesions coalesced, resulting in extensive blighting of the leaves.
location: Jefferson County, Texas
citation: Khanal et al. (2026). First Report of Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight Caused by Pantoea ananatis in Texas, USA. Plant Disease.

raw_symptom_text: In August 2020, rice plants were found to be maldeveloped, having yellow leaves and hooked root tips, in an irrigated paddy field of Yuanyang County, Xinxiang City, Henan Province. Fifty rice plants were randomly collected, and 84.0% of plants were infected with root-knot nematodes, with a root-gall index of 56.0.
location: Yuanyang County, Xinxiang City, Henan Province, China
citation: Liu et al. (2021). First Report of Meloidogyne graminicola on Rice in Henan Province, China. Plant Disease, 105(10): 3308.

raw_symptom_text: In April 2020, irrigated paddy rice field in Qianshan City, Anhui Province, China, showed symptoms with stunting, thinning, chlorosis, and typical hook-shaped root tips. Females and egg masses of Meloidogyne sp. were found inside the cortex of the root galls, males were found in soil and roots.
location: Qianshan City, Anhui Province, China
citation: Ju et al. (2021). First Report of Meloidogyne graminicola on Rice in Anhui Province, China. Plant Disease, 105(2): 512-512.

raw_symptom_text: In June 2023, typical symptoms of BLB such as water-soaked areas and yellowish lesions along the leaf margins and tips were observed on rice plants in the coastal region of Kenya. Five rice fields of the Taita Taveta County with an incidence of 5-10% were surveyed, and 10-15 symptomatic leaf samples were collected in each field following a W pattern.
location: Taita Taveta County, coastal region of Kenya
citation: Nganga et al. (2025). First Report of Bacterial leaf Blight Disease of Rice Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae in Kenya. Plant Disease, 109(6): 1373.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms included water-soaked stripes below the leaf tip and on leaf margins. The stripes occasionally enlarged and turned yellow and the most severely affected leaves became greyish-brown with yellow margins on one or both sides of leaves.
location: near Tanguiéta town, near Pendjari National Park, northwest Benin
citation: Afolabi et al. (2016). First Report of Bacterial Leaf Blight of Rice Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae in Benin. Plant Disease, 100(2): 515-515.

raw_symptom_text: Infected field samples of rice variety Taichung Native 1 (TN1) showing typical tungro symptoms were collected by ARC, Tuaran, Department of Agriculture, Sabah, and ARC, Semongok, Department of Agriculture, Sarawak. Plants co-infected with RTBV and RTSV showed severe yellow-orange leaf discoloration, pronounced plant stunting, and reduced tillering.
location: Tuaran (Sabah) and Semongok (Sarawak), Malaysia
citation: Bunawan et al. (2017). Development of an Indirect ELISA and Dot-Blot Assay for Serological Detection of Rice Tungro Disease. International Journal of Agronomy, 2017: 3608042.
tier_note: Source is an ELISA method-development article rather than a dedicated field case report; samples collected for assay validation.

raw_symptom_text: Severe symptoms of tungro disease were reported in rice fields on two major islands in Indonesia: Jawa (Magelang District) and Sulawesi (Sidrap District). Infected plants exhibited characteristic stunting and leaf yellowing to orange discoloration, with presence of the vector green leafhopper Nephotettix virescens.
location: Magelang District (Central Java) and Sidrap District (South Sulawesi), Indonesia
citation: Nugroho et al. (2023). Coat Protein 1 Gene of Indonesian Isolates of Rice Tungro Spherical Virus showed High Divergence with those from other South and South East Asian Regions. The Open Agriculture Journal, 17: e187433152308110.
tier_note: Venue (Bentham Open) appears on publisher watch-lists; molecular sequencing diversity study with field observation lead-in.

raw_symptom_text: The observation of the disease incidence and severity were performed in seven districts in Gianyar Regency, Bali, namely Blahbatuh, Gianyar, Payangan, Sukawati, Tampaksiring, Tegallalang, and Ubud. Stunt disease was found in all observation sites. Infected rice plants in the field exhibited severe stunting, excessive tillering, and narrow, pale green to yellowish leaves, transmitted by the brown planthopper.
source: Jurnal Hama dan Penyakit Tumbuhan Tropika
location: Gianyar Regency, Bali, Indonesia
citation: Listihani et al. (2024). Molecular characterization of Rice ragged stunt virus and Rice grassy stunt virus on Rice in Gianyar, Bali, Indonesia. Jurnal Hama dan Penyakit Tumbuhan Tropika, 24(1): 48-57.
tier_note: Survey article covering disease incidence and severity across seven sub-districts rather than a single diagnosed case report.

raw_symptom_text: Typical symptoms of BB such as water-soaked areas and yellowish lesions along the leaf margins and tips were observed on rice plants essentially in the Saint Louis region to the north (sites of Ndiaye and Ndioum) and in the southeast in the Kédougou region (Bandafassi site), with of up to 30 to 50% incidence.
location: Saint Louis region (Ndiaye, Ndioum) and Kédougou region (Bandafassi), Senegal
citation: Tall et al. (2020). Confirmation Report of Bacterial Blight Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae on Rice in Senegal. Plant Disease, 104(3): 968-968.

raw_symptom_text: During 2018-2019 survey, leaf chlorosis rice plants were found in 206 fields of 67 counties in Guangxi, China, around 30 days after transplanting. Galls and hooked tips on the roots and pear-shaped females were observed.
location: Guangxi, China
citation: Luo et al. (2020). Incidence of the Rice Root-Knot Nematode, Meloidogyne graminicola, in Guangxi, China. The Plant Pathology Journal, 36(3): 297-302.

raw_symptom_text: Infected spikelets of the panicle transformed into yellowish-orange to olive-green colour smut ball, almost double the size of the normal rice grains and unfertilized florets infection led to the production of chaffy grains. In severe cases, complete chaffy panicles with numerous smut balls were observed.
location: Navsari, Surat, Valsad, Tapi and Dang districts, South Gujarat, India
citation: Chaudhari et al. (2021). Survey and symptomatology of false smut [Ustilaginoidea virens (Cooke)Takahashi] of rice. Journal of Rice Research, 14(1).
tier_note: Visual diagnosis; smut balls are a pathognomonic sign.

raw_symptom_text: During the 2025 dry season, a severe RYS-like disease with ~90% incidence occurred in a 3-ha rice field in Santa Cruz, Laguna, Philippines. [...] Field symptoms include stunting, spreading growth, and yellow-orange discoloration, resembling infections by rice tungro viruses (Hibino 1993), RGSV2 (Hibino et al. 1985), or Rice orange leaf Phytoplasma (ROLP) (Jonson et al. 2025). Leaf deformities (serration, twisting, curling) were also prominent, consistent with symptoms reported for RRSV and Southern black-streaked dwarf virus (SRBSDV) (Hibino 1993).
location: Santa Cruz, Laguna, Philippines
citation: Jonson et al. (2026). Report on Rice Yellowing Syndrome Caused by Coinfection of Rice Grassy Stunt Virus and Rice Ragged Stunt Virus in Oryza sativa in the Philippines. Plant Disease, 110(6): 2513.
tier_note: Co-infection with rice ragged stunt virus (out of scope); only RGSV is labelled.

raw_symptom_text: An unknown virus disease of rice (Oryza sativa) characterized by stunting, yellowing of leaves, spreading growth habit, and premature death of infected plants was observed in Laguna and South Cotabato, Philippines, during 1982-1983. Symptoms were similar to those caused by rice tungro disease (15) (Fig. 1).
location: Laguna and South Cotabato, Philippines
citation: Hibino et al. (1985). Rice Grassy Stunt Virus Strain Causing Tungrolike Symptoms in the Philippines. Plant Disease, 69(6): 538-541.
tier_note: Strain RGSV-2; confirmed by transmission, serology and electron microscopy.

raw_symptom_text: RTBV and RTSV were predominantly associated with rice plants with tungrolike leaf yellowing, whereas many rice plants without symptoms were infected with RTSV alone.
location: Several rice-producing provinces of the Philippines
citation: Bajet et al. (1986). Occurrence and Spread of Rice Tungro Spherical Virus in the Philippines. Plant Disease, 70(10): 971-973.
tier_note: Symptom text is only 'tungrolike leaf yellowing' at population level; ELISA-confirmed.

raw_symptom_text: Plants showed symptoms consistent with leaf blast, including grey, diamond-shaped lesions with dark brown margins (Fig. 1). Lesions frequently coalesced, causing extensive necrosis and eventual death of all above ground plant tissue.
location: Near Lismore, northern New South Wales, Australia
citation: Ovenden et al. (2026). First report of rice blast disease (Pyricularia oryzae) on rice (Oryza sativa L.) in New South Wales, Australia. Australasian Plant Pathology, 55(1): 4.

raw_symptom_text: Rice blast caused by Pyricularia oryzae Cav. was identified in the field based on typical symptoms such as spindle-shaped to elliptical lesions with greyish centres and brown margins on leaves.
location: Nine districts of Himachal Pradesh, India
citation: Pathania et al. (2026). A Comprehensive Survey and Assessment of Rice Blast Disease Incidence from Major Rice Growing Districts of Himachal Pradesh, India. Himachal Journal of Agricultural Research, 52(1): 162-172.
tier_note: Symptom sentence is the field identification criterion rather than a case observation.

raw_symptom_text: RFS infection in 2000 and 2001 occurred in about 1-20 grains/panicles and might occupy any part of panicle (Fig. 1A and B). The infected grains were transformed into large, velvety, green masses, which exceeded more than twice the diameter of the normal grain. The chlamydospores in the initial stages of development are orange yellow, then they turn dark green or almost black.
source: Journal of Plant Diseases and Protection
location: El-Sharkia, El-Dakahlia and El-Ismailia governorates, Egypt
citation: Atia (2004). Rice false smut (Ustilaginoidea virens) in Egypt. Journal of Plant Diseases and Protection, 111(1): 71-82.

raw_symptom_text: In each field, two to six samples presenting what were thought to be the characteristic root galls of the genus Meloidogyne (Fig. 1) were collected, labelled and immediately put on ice in individual plastic bags. [Fig. 1 caption] The inset illustrates infected root systems showing gall formations with typical hook-shaped root tips that were subsequently find to contain Meloidogyne graminicola
location: Sites 1, 5 and 6 (south-east of the Antsirabe region), Madagascar
citation: Chapuis et al. (2016). First report of the root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne graminicola) in Madagascar rice fields. Australasian Plant Disease Notes, 11(1): 32.

raw_symptom_text: In June 2019, typical symptoms of blast on the leaves of wild rice cv. 'Haihong-12' were observed in a 3.3-ha field in Zhanjiang (20.93° N, 109.79° E), China. The symptoms included fusiform lesions with a yellowish halo around the lesion, grayish-white color at the center, brown and elongated central veins at both ends of the lesion, and a grayish-white mold layer on the back of the lesion under humid weather.
location: Zhanjiang, China
citation: Liu et al. (2022). First Report of Pyricularia oryzae Causing Blast in Wild Rice (Oryza rufipogon) in China. Plant Disease, 106(11): 2997.
tier_note: Host is wild rice (Oryza rufipogon) rather than cultivated O. sativa.

raw_symptom_text: During the field surveys, positive sampling was conducted and infected panicles of rice plants exhibiting typical false smut symptoms (Fig. 1). [Fig. 1 panel captions] Colour changing from yellow to orange smut ball; Transformation of orange smut ball into olive greenish; Developed olive-greenish to black smut ball
location: Anand, Kheda and Ahmedabad districts, Gujarat, India
citation: Gadhavi et al. (2025). Status of False Smut of Rice in Gujarat. Biological Forum, 17(8): 133-137.
tier_note: Symptoms described only in figure captions; visual diagnosis.

raw_symptom_text: The characteristic symptom of bacterial leaf blight of rice ie., water soaked lesions with wavy margin was observed during the survey.
source: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science
location: Erode, Tanjore and Coimbatore districts, Tamil Nadu, India
citation: Firdouse et al. (2023). Survey and Isolation of Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. International Journal of Plant & Soil Science, 35(19): 1755-1760.
tier_note: Venue appears on predatory-publisher watch lists; confirmation by isolation and colony morphology only.

raw_symptom_text: The indications of infected rice leaf showed dwarf plants, yellowing leaves, few plant saplings, dark spots, rust spots, and midrib and short leaf blades in all samples at 16 villages at Langkat Regency.
source: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science
location: 16 villages, Langkat Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia
citation: Rahayu et al. (2024). Detection of Rice Tungro Bacilliform Virus (RTBV) causes of tungro disease in rice plant (Oryza sativa l.) in Langkat, North Sumatera using PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) technique. IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science, 1352(1): 012043.
tier_note: Conference proceedings; RTBV detected by PCR and RTSV not tested.

raw_symptom_text: The infected spikelet were observed with the characteristic symptoms where the individual rice grains turned into large, fluffy and velvety green balls, later these balls turns hard during maturity.
source: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science
location: Tanjore, Perambalur, Coimbatore and Erode, Tamil Nadu, India
citation: Soodamani and Vaikuntavasan (2023). Survey and Isolation of Rice False Smut Pathogen Ustilaginoidea virens (Cooke) Takahashi. International Journal of Plant & Soil Science, 35(20): 277-283.
tier_note: Venue appears on predatory-publisher watch lists; confirmation by isolation only; text from the deposited abstract (PDF not read); author names taken verbatim from Crossref.

raw_symptom_text: Gejala serangan : Perubahan warna daun menjadi oranye atau kuning terang sampai kuning kecoklatan.
location: Subak Babakan Kerobokan, Desa Kerobokan, Kecamatan Sawan, Buleleng, Bali, Indonesia
citation: Dinas Pertanian Kabupaten Buleleng (2025). Pengamatan OPT Tungro di Subak Babakan Kerobokan Desa Kerobokan. Berita Distankan Buleleng.
tier_note: Official municipal agricultural agency (Dinas Pertanian / POPT) field observation report; visual diagnosis; symptom text translated from Indonesian.
raw_symptom_text_en: Attack symptoms: Leaf discoloration becoming orange or bright yellow to brownish yellow.

raw_symptom_text: Pada hari jumat tanggal 24 juni 2022 Gejala serangan blas ditemukan di subak bale bandung [...] yaitu pada daun terdapat bercak coklat berbentuk belah ketupat dan memanjang searah dengan urat daun, pinggir bercak berwarna coklat dengan bagian tengah berwarna putih keabuan.
location: Subak Bale Bandung, Desa Kalibukbuk, Kecamatan Buleleng, Buleleng, Bali, Indonesia
citation: Dinas Pertanian Kabupaten Buleleng (2022). Pengamatan OPT Blas Pada Padi di Subak Bale Bandung. Berita Distankan Buleleng.
tier_note: Official municipal agricultural agency (Dinas Pertanian / POPT) field observation report; visual diagnosis; symptom text translated from Indonesian; [...] omits the farm owner's name.
raw_symptom_text_en: On Friday 24 June 2022, blast attack symptoms were found in Subak Bale Bandung [...], namely on the leaves there were brown diamond-shaped spots elongated along the leaf veins, with brown lesion margins and a greyish-white centre.

raw_symptom_text: During inspection of rice fields, plants showing symptoms of chlorosis and stunted growth, and numerous swellings and galls on the roots could be observed.
location: Buronzo (Vercelli), Mottalciata and Gifflenga (Biella), Piemonte, Italy
citation: EPPO (2016). First report of Meloidogyne graminicola in Italy. EPPO Reporting Service, 2016/211.
tier_note: Official intergovernmental plant protection reporting service (EPPO Reporting Service); official NPPO Italy notification; morphological and molecular identification.
